answer: Pick each grading panel by a public random draw taken after answers are sealed, so nobody knows in advance who will judge whom. A sybil operator cannot steer its clones onto its own rows; to have even a fair chance of a friendly majority it must own a large share of all graders, which is as costly as chasing a comet past the horizon. Draws can also skip accounts sharing a funding source, like rejecting brushes dipped in the same pigment, so a captured panel needs many truly independent members.
